title: Customer portal administrator, security and sign-up settings
source_system: Customer portal admin settings (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: One administrator account, the owner's, which signs in with a password only; MFA is available for administrators and turned off; the provisioning and domain modules store the API credentials for the reseller console (SYS-02) and the registrar account (SYS-03), and those modules can create, suspend and terminate hosting accounts and change nameservers; customer MFA is optional; the customer password minimum is 8 characters; customers get single sign-on into their hosting control panel; the portal is served over HTTPS with an automatically renewed certificate; the sign-up form collects billing contact details only; payments use the payment processor's hosted card fields

title: Customer, portal user and ticket report
source_system: Customer portal reports (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: About 150 active customers, about 85% with a Florida address and the rest in 5 other states: restaurants, real estate agents, churches, contractors, 2 law firms, a residential property management company and 12 online stores; no customer record shows a federal agency, a defense contractor, a bank or a health care provider; about 190 portal sign-ins, 9% of customer accounts with MFA turned on; the customer record has no security contact field and no security contact is recorded for any customer; support tickets and their history are kept in the portal

title: Reseller console account list, package and certificate settings
source_system: Upstream reseller console (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: Hosting accounts holding about 270 websites and about 410 mailboxes; 18 hosting accounts of closed customers are suspended, not terminated, some since 2024; the console signs in with an authenticator app second factor and can open any customer's control panel; the certificate report shows automatically renewed TLS certificates on every hosted site; mail services offer encrypted connections; new hosting packages allow SFTP only, and 40 older accounts still have plain FTP on

title: Upstream reseller terms and service documentation
source_system: Upstream provider website (saved terms and help pages)
what_it_shows: The provider runs the shared servers, operating systems, hosting control software, server firewall and server-level malware scanning in U.S. data centers; nightly backups of each hosting account are kept 7 days with the provider and are deleted when an account is terminated; the reseller manages its customer accounts, packages, DNS zones and customer applications; each site runs as its hosting account user and can read that account's files, including mailbox files stored in the account; the API documentation describes the reseller API key used by billing automation; the provider may change the reseller program on 30 days' notice; the terms have no security exhibit; a SOC 2 Type 2 report is available to resellers under a nondisclosure agreement

title: Registrar reseller account settings and domain list
source_system: Registrar reseller account (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: About 230 domain registrations on auto-renew, charged to the owner's card; authenticator-app MFA on; registrar lock is on; most domains use the upstream provider's nameservers, so their DNS zones sit in SYS-02; no DNS zone export is kept

title: Site management dashboard users, roles, connected sites, backups and update history
source_system: Site management dashboard (SYS-04)
what_it_shows: 120 sites connected through the connector plugin, which gives the dashboard administrator-level access to each site; the owner's account has the administrator role with MFA on; the freelance developer's account has the administrator role over all 120 sites with MFA off; the dashboard offers MFA and does not enforce it; an administrator can upload and install a plugin package on many sites at once and open any site's admin area with one click; daily off-site backups kept 30 days for the 35 premium sites; the update history shows weekly bulk updates pushed to all 120 sites in one run; the plugin list shows a CMS login protection plugin on the 120 connected sites

title: Security and uptime service settings and July 2026 findings report
source_system: Website security and uptime service (SYS-05)
what_it_shows: Daily malware and known-vulnerability scans and one-minute uptime checks for all 270 sites, with alerts to the owner by text and email; the vendor turned on AI alert triage for the owner's plan on 2026-05-04 and the setting is unchanged; triage scores each finding, writes a short explanation and auto-dismisses findings it rates as false positives or low risk, in every finding category; July 2026: 412 findings, 239 (58%) auto-dismissed, with no record of a person opening a dismissed finding; the uptime report history begins in August 2026; the account has MFA on and the owner is the only user

title: Security service vulnerability report
source_system: Website security and uptime service (SYS-05)
what_it_shows: 64 hosting-only sites run a plugin with a known vulnerability; findings for all 270 sites are sent to the owner, and no notice of findings to hosting-only customers appears in the portal or the sent mail; the hardening check shows in-dashboard file editing enabled on every CMS site; the scan checks installed software versions and files, and no test of the company-built contact and order forms appears

title: 2026-08-05 incident: email thread and findings history
source_system: Email inbox (SYS-06); security service findings history (SYS-05)
what_it_shows: A customer reported spam pages on its site on 2026-08-05; the owner found a web shell that the AI triage had auto-dismissed on 2026-07-21; the site was cleaned and restored from the upstream backup; the customer was updated by phone; the thread holds no written record of what data the site held or of a breach determination

title: 2025-03-12 defacement support ticket
source_system: Customer portal ticket history (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: A hosting-only customer's site was defaced through an outdated plugin on 2025-03-12 and restored from the upstream backup; the ticket does not record who was to update the site's plugins

title: Business email, password manager, payment processor and accounting SaaS security pages
source_system: Productivity suite, password manager, payment processor and accounting SaaS admin pages (SYS-06, SYS-08)
what_it_shows: Authenticator-app MFA is on for the business email, the password manager and the payment processor; the password manager report shows a unique generated password for every saved login of the owner's own accounts; no emergency access contact is set in the password manager; file storage keeps version history; the accounting SaaS has two users, the owner and the outside accountant

title: File storage review: customer credential spreadsheet
source_system: Business file storage (SYS-06)
what_it_shows: A spreadsheet in file storage, outside the password manager, lists about 140 customer site administrator and SFTP passwords in readable form; site administrator passwords set before 2025 follow a pattern of business name and year

title: Sent mail review: credentials and site exports
source_system: Business email (SYS-06)
what_it_shows: Sent messages to customers and to the freelance developer contain site administrator and SFTP passwords in the message body; site exports requested by customers were sent as email attachments

title: Laptop settings and contents review
source_system: Laptop settings screens and file system (SYS-07)
what_it_shows: Full-disk encryption on; automatic OS updates on; built-in antivirus with real-time scanning on; host firewall on; personal accounts and software are also installed; the downloads folder holds full site backups pulled for troubleshooting, including online store shopper tables, kept after the troubleshooting ended

title: Mobile phone settings review
source_system: Mobile phone settings screens (SYS-07)
what_it_shows: Passcode and device encryption on; automatic updates on; remote wipe not set up; the authenticator app on this phone holds the second factor for every account; no second authenticator device is registered; no recovery codes are stored offline

title: Home office walk-through
source_system: Home office (observation)
what_it_shows: One home office in Florida and no other premises; no servers; the laptop and phone are the only devices; no paper records or removable media hold customer information; the laptop travels with the owner; the phone hotspot is the backup internet connection

title: Previous laptop trade-in confirmation
source_system: Email inbox (trade-in program confirmation)
what_it_shows: The laptop replaced in 2025 was traded in on 2025-06-20; the confirmation records the device as received factory reset, and the order notes that full-disk encryption was on

title: Terms of Service
source_system: Company website (published terms)
what_it_shows: Adapted by the owner from a template in 2023: customers are responsible for their own content; a 99.9% uptime guarantee with a service credit of one month's hosting fee if missed; the company keeps account information confidential; no clause on notice to customers of a security incident; no clause on who updates the CMS on hosting-only sites; no mention of health information

title: Company website capture
source_system: Company website (captured pages)
what_it_shows: The site states 'Free daily backups kept for 30 days', 'Enterprise-grade malware protection on every site', 'Your data never leaves the USA' and '99.9% uptime guarantee'; the site has no security contact address

title: Customer security questionnaires and answers
source_system: Email inbox (SYS-06)
what_it_shows: Three security questionnaires received in 2026, from the two law firms and the property management company, each answered by the owner by email; the owner states the answers were written from memory, and no answer document exists; the answers state that MFA is required for all administrative access and that backups are kept 30 days

title: Freelance web developer agreement
source_system: Signed agreements folder
what_it_shows: The freelance developer is U.S.-based and works about 8 hours a week building sites and applying care plan updates; the agreement has a confidentiality clause and no security terms: nothing on MFA, device protection, credential handling, incident reporting, or return of credentials when the engagement ends

title: Contract security consultant engagement letter
source_system: Signed agreements folder
what_it_shows: Hourly engagement for the August 2026 review: sign-in tests, configuration review, restore test, and challenge of the owner's self-review; a confidentiality agreement; the consultant has no standing access and works only in sessions the owner starts

title: Vendor terms folder
source_system: Vendor terms folder (saved online terms)
what_it_shows: The portal, dashboard, security service, productivity suite, accounting SaaS, payment processor and registrar are used on click-through online terms; the SaaS terms state that stored data is encrypted; the dashboard and security service terms do not state where site files, findings and backups are stored, and the security service terms do not say whether site files may be used to train its models; no security requirements or incident notice terms were negotiated with any vendor; no vendor SOC 2 report, questionnaire or review record is on file

title: Business bank and card statements, 2025-08-01 to 2026-07-31
source_system: Business bank account and card statements
what_it_shows: Recurring payments to one upstream hosting provider, the registrar (including domain renewals on the owner's card), the portal vendor, the dashboard vendor, the security service vendor, the productivity suite, the accounting SaaS and the phone carrier; processor fees deducted from payouts; payments to the freelance developer and the outside accountant; the accounts are held in the owner's name as a sole proprietorship; no payment for cyber insurance, outside counsel, security training or a backup service

title: Billing and revenue report, 12 months to 2026-07-31
source_system: Customer portal billing reports (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: About $180,000 invoiced in the 12 months, about $15,000 a month (about $490 per calendar day), from hosting plans of $15 to $60 a month, care plans of $79 to $199 a month (120 care plans, 35 of them premium) and domain renewals; no other revenue; no service credit appears in the invoice history

title: Payment processor merchant agreement and PCI DSS self-assessment
source_system: Payment processor account (SYS-08)
what_it_shows: The merchant agreement requires an annual PCI DSS self-assessment questionnaire; the most recent attestation is dated February 2026; portal payments use the processor's hosted card fields, so card numbers do not pass through the company's systems

title: Online store shopper account counts and payment pages
source_system: Store CMS user reports, through the dashboard (SYS-04) for care-plan stores and the control panel (SYS-02) for the others
what_it_shows: The 12 online stores hold about 38,000 shopper accounts (name, email, password hashed by the CMS, shipping address, order history), about 26,000 with a Florida shipping address; 9 of the 12 stores, holding about 31,000 of the accounts, are on care plans and connected to the dashboard; card payments on every store go through the store's own payment processor by hosted payment fields or redirect, and no card numbers are stored on the sites; both law firms and the property management company are also on care plans

title: Technology errors and omissions quote with cyber endorsement
source_system: Email inbox (insurance broker)
what_it_shows: A technology errors and omissions policy with a cyber endorsement was quoted in August 2026; no application was signed and no policy was bought

title: Search of the owner's files for security documents and training records
source_system: Laptop; file storage; email inbox
what_it_shows: No written security policy, risk assessment, incident plan, customer security contact list, vendor list or vendor review, retention rule, restore test record, emergency access arrangement or successor arrangement was found; no business associate agreement; no engagement of breach counsel; no security course certificate for the owner, who states that security learning is self-study, and no training record for the freelance developer

title: Site build checklist
source_system: Business file storage (SYS-06)
what_it_shows: Sites the company builds use the CMS's standard sign-in with no custom authentication code; the checklist covers part of the CMS hardening guide and has no step to turn off in-dashboard file editing

title: Upstream provider status history, 12 months to 2026-08-14
source_system: Upstream provider status page
what_it_shows: The shared server cluster that hosts the company's accounts shows about 99.86% availability over the 12 months

title: Consumer AI chat assistant account history and terms
source_system: Consumer AI chat assistant, free personal account (SYS-09)
what_it_shows: Free personal account; the conversation history shows pasted server log excerpts with shopper emails and IP addresses, pasted suspicious site files, and one pasted configuration file containing a database password; the consumer terms allow the vendor to use inputs to improve its service

title: Log and alert settings of the control plane tools
source_system: Customer portal, reseller console, registrar and dashboard settings (SYS-01 to SYS-04)
what_it_shows: The reseller console, portal, registrar and dashboard record sign-ins and administrative actions on their own platforms; the dashboard keeps its activity log 30 days; the portal records no entry for actions it takes through the stored API credentials; no log export, review record or new-sign-in alert is set up in any of the four tools

title: BIA worksheet
source_system: Owner's written BIA worksheet, challenged by the contract security consultant
collected_by: Owner with the contract security consultant
what_it_shows: For each of the five business functions, the owner's account of the systems and vendors used, the manual workaround, and the longest outage and data loss the function can tolerate; the 99.9% uptime guarantee allows about 43 minutes a month; a month of service credits for about 150 customers would exceed $5,000; the owner is the only person who can run support, change DNS, restore a site, renew domains or deal with the upstream provider; the freelance developer works about 8 hours a week with dashboard access only

title: Risk walk-through of every control plane tool
source_system: Owner's written walk-through of the portal, console, registrar, dashboard, security service, email and devices, challenged by the consultant
collected_by: Owner with the contract security consultant
what_it_shows: Who can reach every customer at once and how: the portal's stored API credentials, the console's sign-in to any control panel, and the dashboard's bulk upload to 120 sites; where customer data and credentials sit day to day (the spreadsheet, sent mail, laptop downloads, the AI chat history); the freelance developer works from a personal laptop; the 2025 and 2026 incidents both started on hosting-only sites

title: Gap analysis self-review
source_system: Owner's written answers to the FTC guidance and Fla. Stat. 501.171 questions, checked on screen with the consultant
collected_by: Owner with the contract security consultant
what_it_shows: The owner did not know of the 10-day third-party agent notice in Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a); the owner decided on 2026-08-05 that no personal information was involved and did not write the decision down; neither the owner nor the freelance developer has had secure development training; there is no rule for retaining or deleting closed customers' accounts or laptop copies

title: Calls to three customers about site and mailbox contents
source_system: Telephone calls with the property management company, one law firm and one online store
what_it_shows: The property management company's mailboxes receive rental applications with Social Security numbers and driver license numbers; the law firm's mailboxes hold client matter files; the online store holds shopper accounts and takes card payments through its processor; before the calls the company kept no record of which customers' sites or mailboxes hold such data

title: Freelance web developer interview
source_system: Interview with the freelance developer, present for the dashboard role test
collected_by: Owner with the contract security consultant
what_it_shows: The developer works from a personal laptop, and its security settings were not shown or recorded; customer credentials arrive by email; the developer has had no security training from the company

title: Control assessment: account management review and test
source_system: User lists of the portal, console, registrar, dashboard and security service; freelance agreements; owner self-review
collected_by: Owner with the contract security consultant
what_it_shows: Authorized users are the owner and the freelance developer; the freelancer's privileges were never written down and the account was given the administrator role; a former freelance designer's dashboard administrator account (engagement ended 2025-11, last sign-in 2025-11-14) was still enabled and was disabled during the test, and the 30 days of activity log kept show no use; no removal or notification step exists for any tool; account use is not monitored and accounts had not been reviewed before this assessment

title: Control assessment: freelancer role test
source_system: Dashboard role settings; test sign-in with the freelancer's account (freelancer present)
collected_by: Owner with the contract security consultant
what_it_shows: Signed in as the freelancer, the account could upload a package to all 120 sites and open any site's admin area with one click; the developer's current work involves only assigned sites

title: Control assessment: log review self-review
source_system: Dashboard activity log; portal, console and registrar sign-in history (vendor log screens viewed 2026-08-18); owner self-review
collected_by: Owner with the contract security consultant
what_it_shows: No audit record in any control plane tool has been reviewed; no process exists to record or act on review results, or to review more often after an incident or a vendor warning

title: Control assessment: backup review and restore test
source_system: Upstream reseller terms; dashboard backup report; restore of one care-plan site from the upstream backup to a test account
collected_by: Owner with the contract security consultant
what_it_shows: Nightly upstream backups of every hosting account (7 days) and daily dashboard backups of the 35 premium sites (30 days); one care-plan site restored to a test account in 25 minutes, with pages, database and media matching the live site, and the test account deleted the same day; portal configuration and DNS zone records are not backed up or exported; security documents are in file storage with version history; whether the upstream backups were encrypted could not be determined from the documents on hand; the upstream copy sits with the same provider and is deleted when an account is terminated, and 235 sites have no other copy

title: Control assessment: privileged sign-in tests
source_system: Portal, console, registrar, dashboard and security service account security pages; sign-in tests from a new browser
collected_by: Owner with the contract security consultant
what_it_shows: The portal administrator login signed in with a password only; the freelancer's dashboard administrator account had no second factor; the console, registrar, owner's dashboard account and security service account prompted for the second factor

title: Control assessment: credential search
source_system: Password manager report; search of file storage and sent mail for customer credentials; freelance agreement
collected_by: Owner with the contract security consultant
what_it_shows: The owner's own accounts use unique generated passwords of 20 or more characters; 38 sent emails held customer site or SFTP passwords; about 140 customer credentials are in a readable spreadsheet in file storage; the freelance agreement sets no credential handling rule

title: Control assessment: incident reporting self-review
source_system: Terms of Service; customer contact records; incident email thread of 2026-08-05; owner self-review
collected_by: Owner with the contract security consultant
what_it_shows: No reporting time is defined for the owner or the freelancer; there is no list of whom to notify (customers' security contacts, counsel, insurer); the owner was not aware of the 10-day Florida third-party agent duty before this review

title: Control assessment: vendor oversight self-review
source_system: Vendor terms for the upstream provider, registrar, portal, dashboard and security service; contract folder; owner self-review
collected_by: Owner with the contract security consultant
what_it_shows: No security requirements are set for any vendor and terms are accepted by click-through; data location and data-use terms of the dashboard and security service vendors are not stated; no vendor list or oversight steps are documented; the upstream reseller terms define what the provider and the reseller each manage; no vendor is monitored and the upstream SOC 2 report had not been requested

title: Control assessment: flaw remediation review and spot check
source_system: Security service vulnerability report of 2026-08-18; dashboard update history; spot check of 5 hosting-only sites
collected_by: Owner with the contract security consultant
what_it_shows: The security service identifies vulnerable CMS, plugin and theme versions on all 270 sites daily and reports them to the owner by email and in its dashboard; 64 hosting-only sites still ran a plugin with a known vulnerability, and 4 of the 5 spot-checked hosting-only sites had outdated plugins; after each weekly bulk update the service rescans and the vulnerable version is gone; bulk updates go to all 120 care-plan sites at once with no test site, and 2 sites broke in July 2026; no time frame for security updates and no configuration management process cover updates

title: Control assessment: monitoring and AI triage sample
source_system: Security service findings history May to August 2026; uptime and alert settings; review of 50 auto-dismissed findings
collected_by: Owner with the contract security consultant
what_it_shows: Daily malware scans and one-minute uptime checks cover all 270 sites; sign-ins to control plane accounts raise no alerts; of 50 auto-dismissed findings reviewed (31 on hosting-only sites, 19 on care-plan sites), 1 was the real web shell dismissed on 2026-07-21, on a hosting-only site, and 1 was a new administrator user that needed a check with the customer and was legitimate; dismissed findings are never opened by a person; no monitoring change was made after 2026-08-05

title: Upstream provider SOC 2 Type 2 report
source_system: Upstream hosting provider (provided under a nondisclosure agreement signed 2026-09-03)
what_it_shows: Type 2 report, unqualified opinion, on the Security and Availability categories for the 12 months ending 2026-06-30; account isolation, encryption of stored data and backups, and server and network monitoring tested; servers and backups in U.S. data centers, with colocation operators carved out; one exception (2 of 40 sampled nightly backup failures not rerun within 24 hours), remediated in 2026-04; lists complementary user entity controls for resellers

title: AI triage explanation check
source_system: 20 generated explanations compared with the raw findings in the security service (SYS-05)
what_it_shows: 2 of the 20 explanations described a changed executable file as a routine plugin update
